title: Direct Coupling of Stable High-Level Policy to Volatile I/O
pattern: A high-level policy or core algorithmic function directly instantiates or depends on concrete file system, console, or network I/O mechanisms.
why_bad: High-level policies should be highly stable and reusable. Coupling them directly to I/O devices or system structures makes them volatile and limits their reuse (e.g., encrypting stream data, network sockets, or testing with in-memory buffers).
detection: A module categorized as "Core Domain" or "Policy" imports and directly invokes concrete I/O functions (`std::fs`, `std::net`, `std::io::stdout`).
counterexample: Low-level drivers, CLI main entry points, or infrastructural adapters are expected to bind directly to I/O.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Architecture* (2017), Chapter 19, "Policy and Level", p. 184-187, 280-281.
